meta.tagline: The hill of the gods, the chaos of the streets, and a kefi that never ends

pills: Let the taverna table run long

overview.title: Welcome to Athens
overview.intro: Come expecting a museum and Athens will surprise you: the Acropolis floats at the end of every street, but the simmering city below belongs to today. Third-wave coffee bars under graffiti-covered walls, tavernas overflowing at midnight beside the ancient Agora, orange trees on the pavements and a Mediterranean energy with a Balkan accent. The twenty-five-century city is neither polished nor perfect — but it is real, filling, and once it wins you, it never lets go.

local_word.definition: That hard-to-define Greek exhilaration: the state where music, table and moment merge and lift you. Kefi cannot be planned; it arrives — and on a taverna night in Athens, it will call on you too.

rules.title: Climb the Acropolis at opening time
rules.description: At 8 am the marble is cool, the light golden, the crowds absent. By noon it's queues, heat and a selfie forest. Buy a dated ticket online; in summer there is no shade on bare marble at midday.

rules.title: Pick a neighbourhood, not a highway
rules.description: Athens is a city of neighbourhoods: Plaka's postcard, Koukaki's calm, Exarchia's voice on the walls, Psiri's night. Where you sleep decides which Athens you live.

rules.title: Open the app before hailing a taxi
rules.description: Outside the airport flat rate, meter haggling is a tourist classic; apps like FreeNow end the argument. The metro is fast, cheap and as beautiful as a museum anyway.

tip.label: The Athens philosophy
tip.text: In Athens a plan holds fifty percent; the street fills in the rest. If music starts on a square, sit; if the old man at the next table starts a story, listen — that is the city's curriculum.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The centre walks and the metro carries the rest; arguing with Athens traffic is a war already lost.

items.title: Metro — the underground museum
items.description: Three lines weave the centre and the port; Syntagma and Akropoli stations display finds from their own excavations. M3 to the airport, M1 to Piraeus. One ticket covers the whole network for 90 minutes.

items.title: Walking the centre
items.description: The Dionysiou Areopagitou promenade wraps the Acropolis's foot: Plaka, Monastiraki and Thissio chain together on foot. The city's best 'public transport' is this marble pavement.

items.title: Tram to the coast
items.description: From Syntagma the tram runs down to the Faliro and Glyfada beach line; the cheap, scenic way to see seaside Athens (the Athens Riviera).

items.title: Taxis and apps
items.description: The yellow cabs are cheap, but meter games with tourists are a classic; call by app, pay by card. Airport-centre is a daytime flat rate — mention it before setting off.

items.title: Piraeus for the islands
items.description: If the islands call, take M1 down to Piraeus; Aegina and Hydra are day-trip distance. In summer book ferries ahead and check your gate number.

callout.label: Pedestrian warning
callout.text: In Athens traffic, a green light is advisory: look twice for motorbikes when crossing. And don't be surprised by the scooter parked under an orange tree on the pavement.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Athens the neighbourhood matters more than the hotel; the colour of the walls, the sound of breakfast and the length of the night all change with it.

local_word.definition: The square: the heart of every Athens neighbourhood. Children play ball, elders spin backgammon, cafés overflow. In choosing your neighbourhood you are really choosing your platia.

items.name: Plaka — at the Acropolis's foot
items.description: Neoclassical houses, bougainvillea and the stone steps of Anafiotika: the Athens postcard. Touristy, but justifiably; early morning and late night its magic multiplies. Prices above the city average.

items.name: Koukaki — the calm smart choice
items.description: The quarter behind the Acropolis Museum: the walking distances match Plaka, the prices and quiet are kinder. Its coffee bars and bakeries give the feel of lived-in Athens.

items.name: Monastiraki/Psiri — market and night
items.description: Flea market, rooftop bars and midnight souvlaki queues: the city's most energetic bed. Pick a well-soundproofed room; in return you wake on the pulse of Athens.

items.name: Kolonaki — elegant Athens
items.description: Boutiques, galleries and café terraces at the foot of Lycabettus: the city's polished face. Close to the museum set too (Cycladic, Benaki); quiet nights, graceful days.

items.name: Exarchia — the voice on the walls
items.description: Graffiti, record shops, collective cafés and political history: Athens's rebel quarter. Contrary to cliché, its daytime is creative and warm; for seekers of alternative culture.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Athens has one enemy — the July heat — and nearly every other month for a friend.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Orange Blossom
items.subtitle: Spring · Blossom scent, ideal warmth
items.description: The streets smell of orange blossom, the ancient sites are walkable, the terraces are open. Coincide with Greek Easter and candlelit nights and lamb feasts come as a bonus.

callout.label: Easter tip
callout.text: On Greek Easter night (the date shifts) the churches drown in candlelight; at the cry of 'Christos Anesti' the fireworks go up — being in the city is luck itself.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Heat and Stage
items.subtitle: Summer · 35°C+, open-air festival
items.description: The midday heat is merciless, but at night the city spills into open-air cinemas and concerts at the Herodion. In August Athenians flee to the islands; the city is left to visitors, and some shops take holidays.

callout.label: Heat warning
callout.text: In July and August tour the ancient sites between 8 and 11, save midday for a museum or the sea; water bottle and hat are non-negotiable.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: The Golden Season
items.subtitle: Autumn · Warm sea, empty ruins
items.description: September and October are Athens at its peak: the sea still swims, the light softens, the crowds recede. Even November feels like most of Europe's spring — the terraces stay open.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In October take the tram to Vouliagmeni: a swim in the thermal lake plus a seaside lunch — holiday feeling half an hour from town.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Locals' Athens
items.subtitle: Winter · Quiet ruins, full cafés
items.description: You walk the Acropolis nearly alone, the museums are yours, the taverna stoves are lit. A walkable winter apart from rain breaks; prices at their kindest.

callout.label: Winter tip
callout.text: The winter street markets (laiki) with their mandarin mountains and olive stalls are the city's most colourful sight; ask your hotel which day is market day.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Athens table is generous: meze beyond the table's edge, charcoal-scented meat, and a free dessert arriving with the bill.

local_word.definition: 'Stuffed': tomatoes and peppers above all — the summary of the home-cooking tradition. The trays in the taverna's glass counter (magirefta) are the day's home dishes — ask, point, choose.

items.name: Souvlaki and gyros
items.description: The city's national fast food: skewered meat or shaved gyros, wrapped in pita with tomato, onion and tzatziki. The place with a midnight queue is the right place.

items.name: Horiatiki — the real Greek salad
items.description: No lettuce, giant tomatoes and one solid slab of feta: that's the true version, finished with oil and oregano. Summer's unchanging first plate.

items.name: Grilled octopus and gavros
items.description: The two poles of the sea meze: charred octopus with vinegar, crisp anchovies with lemon. They come in sequence with ouzo or tsipouro; nobody hurries you.

items.name: Tiropita and spanakopita
items.description: The cheese and spinach pies are the morning stars of the bakery window; breakfast standing, pie in hand, Acropolis across the way — that's the Athens manner.

items.name: Paidakia — lamb chops over charcoal
items.description: A mountain of chops on paper, with fries and lemon; the pride plate of the meat tavernas (hasapotaverna). Kefi usually begins after this dish.

items.name: Galaktoboureko and loukoumades
items.description: Syrupy custard pie and honeyed doughnuts: the two champions of dessert. In most tavernas dessert arrives free anyway — if it doesn't, ask for one of these.
items.tag: Patisserie or taverna · await the treat

callout.label: The taverna rule
callout.text: If the waiter starts reciting 'today we have...' instead of handing a menu, you're in the right place. Go to the counter, look in the pots, point — in Athens this is not rude, it is expertise.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone knows the Acropolis; these six corners are what make you love Athens the second time.

items.rarity: A neighbourhood moved from an island
items.name: Anafiotika
items.description: Above Plaka, a tiny whitewashed quarter built by Cycladic craftsmen in the 19th century: narrow passages, blue doors, a forest of flowerpots. An island holiday in the middle of Athens.

items.name: Lycabettus Hill
items.description: 277 metres by funicular or footpath: the whole city from the Acropolis to the sea at your feet. Go up for sunset, see the chapel, come down as the lights turn on.

items.name: Kerameikos
items.description: Ancient Athens's cemetery and Sacred Gate: cypresses, tortoises and marble stelae in the city's most peaceful site. The crowds never come here.

items.name: The Monastiraki flea market
items.description: Everything from records to brass coffee pots around Avissinias Square: on Sunday mornings, the city's most entertaining theatre of haggling. Walk it whether you buy or not.

items.name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation (SNFCC)
items.description: Renzo Piano's opera-library complex and its great park: the sea from the roof terrace, free events in the evenings. Half an hour by tram to the summit of modern Athens.

items.rarity: A thermal lake at the city's edge
items.name: Lake Vouliagmeni
items.description: A warm thermal lake cradled by rock walls on the Riviera: 22 degrees even in winter, tiny fish within. Half an hour from town, a week's holiday for the soul.

callout.label: Museum tip
callout.text: Under the Acropolis Museum's glass floors an ancient neighbourhood lies at your feet; on Friday nights it stays open late, and the restaurant terrace gives one of the Parthenon's best evening views for free.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Athens's traps are old-school and familiar; know these four and the rest of the city deals honestly.

items.name: The 'traditional taverna' with a doorway hawker in Plaka
items.description: Where the menu is waved and the sentence starts with 'my friend', frozen moussaka arrives at tourist prices; even the music is on tape.
items.instead: Turn into the hawker-free lanes: the back streets of Psiri, or the tavernas of Petralona and Pangrati serve the same food at half the price, in its real form.

items.name: The airport meter 'malfunction'
items.description: Outside the flat rate, 'night tariff' and 'luggage fee' games multiply the bill.
items.instead: State the daytime flat rate before setting off, or take the M3 metro in 40 minutes; an app booking ends the debate before it starts.

items.name: The 'free shot' bar and the bill shock
items.description: Around Monastiraki, some bars open with a 'welcome shot' and close with a bill padded by items not on any menu.
items.instead: Never sit where the price list isn't visible; if you want a rooftop, choose it for its view and its menu, not its tout.

items.name: 'Licensed guide' bargaining at the site gates
items.description: Some of the 'licensed guides' who approach at the gate are neither licensed nor guides; you pay dearly for a memorised script.
items.instead: If you want a guide, book a licensed one ahead; otherwise walk the Acropolis at your own pace in the morning and let the museum complete the story.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: In Athens, a sentence starting 'my friend' is commerce and a sentence starting 'ela' is warmth. The day you tell them apart, the city treats you differently.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From the hill to the taverna, an Athens digest

steps.title: Acropolis — at the gates' opening
steps.description: See the Parthenon in morning light, without the crowds; greet the caryatids of the Erechtheion.

steps.title: The Acropolis Museum
steps.description: Glass floors and the Parthenon frieze; the story of what you saw on the hill completes itself here.

steps.title: Plaka + Anafiotika
steps.description: Lunch in a quiet corner of Plaka, then lose yourself in Anafiotika's whitewashed passages.

steps.title: Ancient Agora + Monastiraki
steps.description: From the shade of the Temple of Hephaistos to the noise of the flea market: two thousand years in a fifteen-minute walk.

steps.title: Lycabettus sunset
steps.description: Funicular to the top; a bird's-eye farewell to the Acropolis as the city turns crimson.

steps.title: Taverna night in Psiri
steps.description: Meze, paidakia, house wine; if live music starts, don't resist the kefi.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the city as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: The ancient centre
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: Acropolis, museum, Plaka, Lycabettus, Psiri.

steps.title: Market, walls and the modern shore
steps.description: The Monastiraki flea market and Kerameikos in the morning, a fish taverna at the central market (Varvakios) at noon, Exarchia's walls and record shops in the afternoon, sunset and a free event at the SNFCC at night.

steps.title: Riviera or island escape
steps.description: Either tram to Vouliagmeni: thermal lake + sea + a shore lunch; or ferry from Piraeus to Aegina: pistachios, an ancient temple and a harbour taverna. A farewell meze in Koukaki on return.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Three words of Greek start the free treats at a taverna; five words start a friendship.

items.meaning: Hello / goodbye — the formal, safe greeting
Thank you — looks hard, lands by the second try
Please / you're welcome — Greek's joker card
Cheers! — ouzo and wine glasses rise to this
'Come / come on / no way!' — the magic Greek word that fits every feeling
